lever: flagvals: one line appended to the Rules of prompts/system.md: a new on/off option or environment variable: if the issue says it adds to or mirrors an existing one, git grep that one in the source and tests/ and treat its values the same way; otherwise "1" turns it on, "0" turns it off, and any other value (unset, empty, unknown) keeps today's behaviour, unless the issue defines the values.
why: Mechanism (HIDDEN_SPEC, guessable): the issue gives only the variable's name. All six box runs wrote the same patch, the adjacent FORCE_COLOR block's shape ('any value at all means a terminal': if force_color is not None or tty_compatible is not None: return True), and checked only the value 1; four of them submitted at 52-72 s with over 200 s unused (scripts/forty_two/rich_solve/patch_lines.py). Measured on the base snapshot with the hidden test applied (scripts/forty_two/rich_solve/ev_flagvals.py): the rule's convention (1 -> terminal without calling isatty, 0 -> not a terminal, anything else including empty keeps auto-detect) passes the hidden test and all 99 tests of tests/test_console.py; the any-value shape fails it. It is also what both L4 solves wrote (g4-l4-v4, g4-l4-v9-eog, in under 65 s). The issue names no sibling, so the rule's default branch applies, which keeps the model off the FORCE_COLOR template. Evidence: docs/forty_two/evidence/rich_solve_flagvals.txt. Applies outside the 42: held-out loguru_bc2ec9a ('Support FORCE_COLOR'), whose hidden tests require 1 -> on and an empty value -> not applied, the rule's convention; 22 of the 1,044 valid held-out tasks change a line that reads an environment variable (reach.py envflag).
expected: maybe-to-likely: the guess is the whole difficulty and the rule makes it; placement before isatty is the remaining risk (the hidden test checks that 1 does not call isatty)
baseline: p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024), p4_v0t2 (v0-think) all failed with the identical any-value patch; 2 of 12 Kaggle L4 runs solved
regression_risk: 82 tokens on every call. Its subject is rare in the public set: 3 of the 74 gold patches change an environment-variable read, all three in the 42 (rich_3675, rich_3777, rich_3930), so none of the 32 tasks we solve sometimes is about a new flag value (measured, reach.py). The inferred risk is over-reading 'option' as any new boolean parameter (1/0 do not apply to bools, so the line should be inert there), and hidden tasks whose spec really is 'any non-empty value' and is stated only in a link (the 'unless the issue defines the values' clause covers stated specs only).
box_risk: Text-call leaks are not new (10 leaked replies over the six earlier box runs, all recovered after the nudge); new on the v13 screen is one first-reply leak that never recovered (fastapi_14487), cause undecided, v13 not treated as broken. This bundle inherits v13's fenced heredoc in step 3; the added line has no fenced block, backtick, brace or tool-call-shaped text (pinned by tests/test_v13_rich_solve.py). A sample with 0 tool calls points at the base, not at this lever.
